paragraphs.heading: F-16 Nose Landing Gear
paragraphs.text: Interactive Electronic Technical Manual (IETM) for the F-16 nose landing gear assembly. The manual combines descriptive data, an interactive Illustrated Parts Data (IPD) module and step-by-step procedures, all linked to the 3D model.

paragraphs.heading: How to use
paragraphs.text: Select a data module in the publication tree. Click a part in the 3D view or a row in the parts list to cross-highlight it. Use the viewer toolbar to isolate, hide, x-ray or explode the assembly. Add parts to the order list with the cart button.

paragraphs.heading: Data status
paragraphs.text: This is a proof-of-concept publication. Part numbers, CAGE codes and procedures are sample data.

paragraphs.heading: General
paragraphs.text: The nose landing gear supports the forward fuselage on the ground, steers the aircraft during taxi and retracts forward into the nose gear bay in flight.

paragraphs.heading: Strut and swivel
paragraphs.text: The strut housing (10) carries the trunnion. The main swivel arm (20) and strut collar (30) let the strut rotate during retraction.

paragraphs.heading: Steering
paragraphs.text: The steering assembly (40) transfers servo input through the servo link (90), the upper and lower steering links (70, 80) and the steering top head (60) to the steering collar (50).

paragraphs.heading: Retraction
paragraphs.text: The retraction actuator (110) drives the main and secondary actuator arms (120, 130). The gear rotation link (150) swings the strut forward while the folding drag brace (160) breaks over-centre.

paragraphs.heading: Wheel
paragraphs.text: The wheel (230) runs on the hub (220), which is carried in the fork (210).

steps.title: Preliminary requirements
steps.text: Make sure the aircraft is on jacks and the nose wheel is clear of the ground. Install the landing gear ground safety pins.
steps.warning: WARNING: Do not remove the wheel unless the aircraft is safely supported on jacks. The aircraft can fall and cause injury.

steps.title: Identify the wheel and fork assembly
steps.text: Find the wheel and fork assembly (200). Examine the area around the fork for loose or missing parts.

steps.title: Remove the wheel
steps.text: Release the axle retaining hardware. Pull the wheel (230) out of the fork (210). Put the wheel on a clean, padded surface.

steps.title: Remove the hub
steps.text: Remove the hub (220) from the fork. Do not damage the bearing seats.
steps.caution: CAUTION: Keep the bearings clean. Contamination can cause early bearing failure.

steps.title: Examine the fork
steps.text: Examine the fork (210) for cracks, corrosion and damage to the axle bores.

steps.title: Close-up
steps.text: Removal is complete. To install the wheel, do these steps in reverse order: select Restore to put the parts back.

steps.title: Access
steps.text: Make sure that the hydraulic and electrical power is off and that the steering servo is not powered.

steps.title: Servo link
steps.text: Examine the servo link (90) for bending, and the rod ends for free play.

steps.title: Upper and lower steering links
steps.text: Examine the upper (70) and lower (80) steering links. Measure the bushing free play.
steps.caution: CAUTION: The maximum permitted free play is 0.2 mm. Replace the links if the free play is more than this.

steps.title: Steering collar and head
steps.text: Turn the steering collar (50) by hand through its full travel. It must move smoothly and not bind. Examine the steering top head (60).

steps.title: Close-up
steps.text: Record the results in the maintenance log.

steps.title: Preparation
steps.text: Put the aircraft on jacks. Make sure that the nose gear bay is clear of people and equipment.
steps.warning: WARNING: Keep clear of the gear bay during retraction. The moving parts can cause serious injury.

steps.title: Down-lock check
steps.text: Make sure that the folding drag brace (160) is over-centre and the actuator (110) is fully extended.

steps.title: Retract the gear
steps.text: Operate the retraction actuator. The gear rotation link (150) swings the strut forward into the bay. Watch for interference.

steps.title: Extend the gear
steps.text: Extend the gear. Make sure that the drag brace locks over-centre and that the indicator shows down and locked.

steps.title: Close-up
steps.text: Remove the jacks and the safety pins after the test is complete.
